issues.failure_explanation: The error bound uses |sup_{S^d} f| (the absolute value of the supremum of f) rather than ‖f‖_∞ = sup |f|. For any nonzero f ≤ 0 with sup f = 0 (e.g., f = −x₁² on S^d), the right-hand side is 0, so the definition forces exact averaging of f. The notion is therefore far stronger than intended and effectively reduces to exact t-design for many polynomials. All proofs that bound |f(x)| by |sup f| (e.g., the equality in rmk:changec) and the L^p computation equating ‖f‖_p with (∫|sup f|^p dσ)^{1/p} are wrong as written. Replacing |sup f| by ‖f‖_∞ throughout repairs every downstream step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |sup_{S^d} f| with ‖f‖_∞ = sup_{S^d}|f| in Definition def:design and adjust the L^p display to use |f|^p inside the integral. All existing proofs then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Every formal result about (ε,c)-approximate t-design curves — Lemmas lem:overlap and lem:smooth, Theorems thm:const, thm:main, thm:even, and Proposition pro:caps — is false as stated because the definition forces exact averaging of polynomials with sup f = 0. All guarantees about ε_t-approximate t-design curves and Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund families become unreliable.
issues.title: Approximate-design definition uses |sup f| instead of ‖f‖_∞
issues.why_classification: The fix is a single definition-level correction (moving the absolute-value bars). After it, every proof and guarantee survives with no new lemma, construction, or reoptimization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: such a curve is given by the weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:S3stitch prescribes r = (t′+1)s − ⌊(t′+1)s⌋ with t′ = 4t−1, giving r = 4ts − ⌊4ts⌋. Formula (3) instead uses r = 4πts − ⌊4πts⌋, tracing α approximately 4πt ≈ 12.57t times instead of 4t times. The resulting curve has a different length from the claimed 2π√(32t⁴−8t²+1), so the length and minimality claims in the d = 3 case of Theorem thm:weight are not established by the stated formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 4πts − ⌊4πts⌋ with 4ts − ⌊4ts⌋ in formula (3) to match the substitution prescribed by Theorem thm:S3stitch with t′ = 4t−1.
issues.overall_effect: The d = 3 explicit construction in Theorem thm:weight does not produce a curve of the claimed length; the formula-level promise about arc length C ≥ 2π√(32t⁴−8t²+1) is unreliable.
issues.title: Explicit S³ curve formula (3) has spurious factor of π in r
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced formula change visible from Theorem thm:S3stitch's parameter r; after it the construction and length computation are consistent, with no further repair needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a constant $D_t\in 2\Bbb Z$ such that for any $d\in\Bbb N_+$ and $D\geq\pi D_td^{t-1}$
there exists a weighted $t$-design set on $S^d$ of size at most $D_td^{t-1}$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states the condition D ≥ πD_t d^{t-1} (matching Dillon's size bound D_t d^{t-1}), but the proof writes D > πD_t t^d — an entirely different expression that does not match the cited result or the theorem in any parameter regime. Additionally the proof cites a weighted t-design set on S^d rather than S^{d-1} (the domain required by Theorem thm:weightconst), and uses a strict inequality where the theorem uses ≥. In regimes where t^d ≫ d^{t-1} (e.g., d = 2, t = 3) the proof's condition is strictly more restrictive and does not establish the theorem; in the opposite regime the proof's condition is vacuous for small D where the theorem still claims existence.

failure_location.quote: Then, for any $D>\pi D_tt^d$, we may pick smooth $M:[0,1]\to O(d)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace t^d with d^{t-1} (or (d−1)^{t-1}) in the proof's condition, change > to ≥, and correct the design set to reside on S^{d-1} so that Theorem thm:weightconst applies.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:weightstrength — existence of weighted t-design curves of prescribed length D ≥ πD_t d^{t-1} on S^d — is not proved as stated in many (d, t, D) parameter regimes.
issues.title: Proof of thm:weightstrength uses wrong expression πD_t t^d
issues.why_classification: Each correction is a local formula/inequality fix forced by the theorem statement and the cited Dillon result. After these fixes the existing construction argument proves the theorem without any new lemma or changed conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $w_{X,M}$ constructed as in Section \ref{sec:weight} is a weighted $t$-design curve on $S^d$ of length greater than or equal to $\pi|X|$

issues.failure_explanation: On the i-th interval [Λ_{i−1}, Λ_i] the written formula gives w_ℝ(s) = (−1)^i(2(s−Λ_{i−1})−1), whose range has length 2λ(x_i), not the full [−1,1]. The proof's change of variables maps each piece to [−1,1] with Jacobian λ(x_i)/2 — consistent only with the corrected formula w_ℝ(s) = (−1)^i(2(s−Λ_{i−1})/λ(x_i) − 1). With the written formula the curve does not reach the poles at s = Λ_i (so the claimed self-intersection/singularity set is wrong) and the integral identity used in the proof fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2(s−Λ_{i−1})−1 with 2(s−Λ_{i−1})/λ(x_i)−1 in formula (5) so the latitude parameter covers [−1,1] on each piece, matching the Jacobian in the proof and the explicit formulas (2)–(3).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:weightconst as stated (for the curve defined by formula (5)) is unproven; Theorems thm:weight (general d) and thm:weightstrength, which invoke it, inherit the defect.
issues.title: Construction w_{X,M} formula (5) omits 1/λ(x_i) normalization
issues.why_classification: A single forced formula correction restores the change of variables, the singularity analysis, and every downstream use of Theorem thm:weightconst, with no new argument required.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed bound W_t ≤ (|Y_t|−1)ρ_t/4 has a wrong constant: W_t is twice the MST total weight of |Y_t| points on CP^n, which is of order (|Y_t|−1)ρ_t with a constant much larger than 1/8 in general (e.g., for well-spread points on CP^1 ≅ S² the MST weight is ≍ √(|Y_t|) while (|Y_t|−1)ρ_t/8 ≍ √(|Y_t|)/4). More importantly, the proof claims ε_t ≍ 1/t but only establishes the upper bound ε_t ≲ 1/t (via W_t ≲ t^{2n−1}). The lower bound ε_t ≳ 1/t requires W_t ≳ t^{2n−1}, i.e., a lower bound on the MST total weight of |Y_t| ≍ t^{2n} well-spread points on the 2n-dimensional manifold CP^n — a non-trivial result that is neither cited nor proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the constant in the W_t upper bound to some C_n(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t and supply a lower bound W_t ≳ (|Y_t|−1)ρ_t (e.g., via a standard MST-weight lower bound on compact 2n-manifolds, using that design sets are well-spread with covering radius ≍ 1/t) to establish ε_t ≍ 1/t.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:main's headline claim ε_t ≍ 1/t (both upper and lower bounds) is unproven; Theorem thm:even, which depends on thm:main through Proposition pro:caps, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Proof of thm:main has wrong W_t bound and no lower bound for ε_t ≍ 1/t
issues.why_classification: Fixing the upper-bound constant is local, but establishing the matching lower bound W_t ≳ t^{2n−1} (needed for ε_t ≍ 1/t as advertised) requires a contained non-trivial argument or citation beyond what the proof provides. The asymptotic rate itself survives once that argument is added, so this is moderate rather than serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The key identity ∫_L f ds = ∫_{γ|_l} f + ∫_{L∖γ(l)} f ds equates the integral over the image subset γ(l) ⊂ L with the parametrized arc-length integral over γ|_l. These are equal only when γ|_l covers γ(l) with multiplicity exactly one. For a general closed curve with self-intersections that revisits parts of L, the parametrized integral counts multiplicity and the identity fails, making the error bound ε_γ = ε + c(|L| + ℓ(γ) − 2ℓ(γ|_l)) too small (it should also account for the excess length ℓ(γ|_l) − |γ(l)| ≥ 0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that γ|_l covers γ(l) exactly once (e.g., γ is simple, or γ|_l is injective) to Lemma lem:overlap. Alternatively, replace the error bound with ε + c(|L| + ℓ(γ) − 2|γ(l)|) to account for multiplicity. All main-theorem applications use simple curves and survive either fix.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:overlap's stated generality (any continuous piecewise-smooth closed curve with finitely many self-intersections) is unsupported. Lemma lem:smooth, which invokes it to smooth non-simple curves and to remove self-intersections for d ≠ 2, inherits an incorrect error bound in those cases. The main theorems (which use simple curves, where the decomposition is valid) are not affected.
issues.title: Lemma lem:overlap decomposition fails for non-simple curves
issues.why_classification: Restricting to the injective-overlap case (or adjusting the bound by a multiplicity term) is a short local repair that preserves every substantive claim used in the main theorems, with no new lemma or replacement argument needed.
